title: Poison-Swallowing Mutex Fallbacks
pattern: A lock acquisition operation (such as Mutex lock) handles lock poisoning/failure by silently returning a default "safe" fallback value (like 0 or empty string) instead of propagating the failure.
why_bad: A poisoned lock means a thread panicked while holding the lock, likely leaving the shared state partially mutated and corrupted. Swallowing the poison error and continuing to read/write that corrupted data pollutes the system state silently and leads to downstream logical bugs.
detection: `lock()` calls that match `Err(_)` branches and return a dummy literal or constant without propagating the error or panicking.
fix: Fail fast. Panic on poisoned locks using `.expect()` or `.unwrap()`, or propagate the failure safely, ensuring that the system does not run with corrupted memory.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 10 (Mutex poisoning and unwinding panic cascades).
